title: unbundle-legacy-ssl-and-harden-jwt-saml-parsers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Several runtime images and the SSO bridge still ship against a bundled OpenSSL 1.1.x ABI and older JWT/SAML parsing libraries. Recent transitive CVEs in XML parsing and JWT token validation mean we have to both upgrade native crypto to OpenSSL 3.1 and remediate fragile token parsing code paths. Scope: - Remove bundled OpenSSL artifacts from runtime base images and rebuild against OpenSSL 3.1 (musl and glibc build matrix) - Upgrade primary JWT libraries (node/jsonwebtoken, python/jose) to patched, audited versions and add stricter token validation rules (strict alg checks, exp/nbf enforcement, key id mismatch handling) - Replace fragile SAML xmlsec usage with a hardening wrapper that enforces schema validation, namespace normalization, and limits entity-size to avoid billion laughs/XXE vectors - Introduce JWK rotation playbook: automatic key discovery, cached JWK with TTL, backoff/fetch error fallback to existing signing key during rollout - Add automated fuzzing/integration tests for auth paths and a smoke SSO harness that runs against canary cluster - Compatibility shim: for older customer kernels where OpenSSL 3.1 build fails, ship a slim shim that surfaces a limited, audited crypto surface while blocking deprecated API paths Rollout plan and acceptance criteria: - Stage 1 (canary): build new runtime images and deploy to a small dedicated pool running internal infra tests; validate API token issuance and SSO login flows - Stage 2 (beta customers): opt-in dedicated pools and a handful of enterprise customers with SSO enabled - Stage 3 (full): phased rollout across hosted fleet with circuit-breaker to fallback to legacy token adapter only for affected tenants if regressions seen Acceptance: no regression in baseline P50 latency for short generation requests (+/-5%), all CI auth tests pass, no SSO failures in canary for 72h, security review sign-off and checklist complete.
comments: 2026-01-19 — Triage: flagged as high priority after security advisory; assigned initial owner (Marco). Will coordinate with infra and security.
2026-01-27 — Design sync: decided on OpenSSL 3.1 due to long-term support and FIPS alignment. Avoid BoringSSL substitution because of downstream 3rd-party binary compatibility.
2026-02-02 — Trade-offs: full rebuild of several base images increases CI time by ~30%. Mitigation: cache compiled wheels and cross-compile artifacts in build farm.
2026-02-18 — PR 8742 opened: initial OpenSSL 3.1 build for glibc images. Early failures in musl variant due to missing EVP APIs — working with toolchain team.
2026-02-25 — Security review scheduled for 2026-03-05. PM requested clearer JWK rotation rollback steps to notify customers on key-change events.
2026-03-05 — Security review completed: requested stricter token header validation, add unit tests for malformed kid/JWS segments, and require telemetry for key fetch errors.

2026-03-08 — Integration tests: SSO harness intermittently fails for large assertion payloads. Root cause: xml parser default entity handling. Implemented size limits and disabled external entity expansion in wrapper.
2026-03-10 — Canary deploy started to qa-canary cluster. Monitoring channels and posterity dashboard created. Next: monitor for 72h, gather telemetry about token verification latency and error rates.
notes: Implementation owners: Marco (build/runtime), Leena Kapoor (auth), Tomas Ortega (security)
QA checklist: end-to-end SSO login, token introspection, refresh token flows, multi-tenant key rollover test
Rollforward plan: if critical regressions occur, automatic routing to legacy-token-adapter for affected tenants, with 1h rollback window
Observability: add auth-route tracing tags, JWK fetch success/failure counters, and per-issuer failure alarms
